text: You used AI to make that, didn't you? He says, you used AI to make that, didn't you? He says it like he found a knife in a lunch box, like the essay has fingerprints like somewhere behind a paragraph, a machine is wearing the student's face. Yes, I say, good, that's the point. In this classroom, AI is not contraband, it is not the magic box where thought goes to die, it is chalk, it is oxygen, it is the strange second mouth in the wall that answers when language strikes it. Other teachers say, don't touch it. They confuse hiding the tool with mastering the tool. My rule is different. Touch it. Use it openly, use it hard. Use it until the first answer embarrasses you. You want to know what AI makes, used badly, it makes couriers. Students carrying sealed packages from prompt box to grade book. Used well, it makes wrestlers, students who say no, not that voice, not that structure, you miss the hinge try again. That is not cheating. That is thought with the lights on. A prompt is not a sentence. A prompt is a seed packet. You drop words into a greenhouse fed by old SA's screenshots, myths, ads, prayers, errors, and ghosts. Something sprouts, usually garbage. Good, now garden. Cut the branch, move the light, name the mold, stake the stem, plant again. A bad prompt asks for fruit. A good... The prompt grows roots. That is the work, not avoidance, fluency, not panic, fluency, not proving you suffered in the approved costume, fluency. I want the mess, the prompt log, the bad output, the failed version, the repair note, because writing is no longer only writing. Writing is designing the room where writing happens. is a lever. Context is a lever. Task is a lever. Format is a lever. Revision is a lever. So the assignment must earn its life. No more museum tasks. No more summarize this and shock when the machine summarizes. If AI defeats your assignment, maybe the assignment was already AI does not remove struggle. It relocates it from sentence to system, from draft to architecture, from private panic to visible process. So when someone says, you used AI to make that, didn't you? I want the student to say, yes, here is the prompt, here is the failure, here is the revision, Here is the bias I found. Here is the part I rejected. Here is where it shaped me back. I did not dodge the struggle. I moved it at the P dot solve 25 to where the real work was hiding. That is what AI makes. Mirrors. Mud. levers, compost. It makes students harder to fool. It makes teachers harder to excuse. It makes assignments show their bones. So answer me. What is your assignment make? Obedience? Or fluency? Concealment? Or disclosure? Polished compliance? Or sharper hands? That is what I'm after. Not clean hands. Better hands. Hands that know the tool. Hands that know the mud. Hands that can build, break, repair, and answer for what they made.
